caption: I know exactly what's due and when. I still couldn't tell you where the R450 in airtime goes. Is that normal on a security guard's salary?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R7 800
p/m salary
Living in Tembisa
slides.body:
Female, 29
Single, staying with her mother
Job: Security officer, night shift
Net salary: R7 800 p/m

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the mall in Kempton Park and back, six nights a week
slides.body: Night shift taxis cost more and there's no way around it.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: My mother's electricity, my little brother's school shoes
slides.body: I'm the only one working full time, so it's not really a choice.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Maize meal, veg, whatever my mom doesn't grow in the yard
slides.body: I shop at month end, then again a week later when the money's already gone.

slides.title: Airtime & data
slides.includes: WhatsApp, TikTok, calling my mom when I'm on shift
slides.body: I could probably halve this. I don't want to.

slides.title: Uniform & work costs
slides.includes: Dry cleaning, shoe polish, a torch that keeps dying
slides.body: Nobody warns you a security job has its own running costs.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Funeral policy, stokvel, toiletries, prepaid electricity for my own room, church offering
slides.body: Six small things. None of them optional, all of them due before the fifteenth.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R7 800. That's under R20 a day until the 25th. I've learned not to plan anything in that window.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of bank statements to Beyond Horizon and finally saw where the R7 800 actually goes.

The airtime number was the one I didn't want to see.

No bank login needed.
